page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 8 virtual and 8 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, containing 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier. For AI workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 402.56 tokens per second on small 135M parameter LLM models, while prompt processing for the same model size remains in the average tier.

The shared CPU allocation provides a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads, allowing users to leverage the NVIDIA L4 GPU and 64 GB of RAM without the cost overhead of dedicated CPU cores. Given the lack of local storage and the high single-core CPU and GPU capabilities, this server is suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-scale LLM inference, machine learning model development, and single-threaded data processing tasks that rely on external storage systems.
